<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/kernel.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2038c56ec99a60e2bf3cb6ee56ef70a5c368ed32`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/kernel.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2038c56ec99a60e2bf3cb6ee56ef70a5c368ed32` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9e414459fa4556f71c88a815fc6e87c16caafbdd` — the merge of head `559cf50443f54565dd625a39bc3aff0e6fb1a759` into base `2038c56ec99a60e2bf3cb6ee56ef70a5c368ed32`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9e414459fa4556f71c88a815fc6e87c16caafbdd && git checkout 9e414459fa4556f71c88a815fc6e87c16caafbdd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2038c56ec99a60e2bf3cb6ee56ef70a5c368ed32 559cf50443f54565dd625a39bc3aff0e6fb1a759 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2038c56ec99a60e2bf3cb6ee56ef70a5c368ed32 && git merge --no-ff 559cf50443f54565dd625a39bc3aff0e6fb1a759

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2038c56ec99a60e2bf3cb6ee56ef70a5c368ed32
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2038c56ec99a60e2bf3cb6ee56ef70a5c368ed32` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `24375ec421c30b753b543f58a6e1727eca34dd2b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts (the gate that enforces the rule, read as one change), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/feature-gate-guard.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts and packages/spec/src/ui/action.form.ts (the precedent), packages/spec/src/data/field-group-layout.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts (SCOPE_ROOTS), ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx, ui/packages/react/src/hooks/useExpression.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (the `multiOrgEnabled` producer), and the new pins in packages/spec, packages/lint and packages/platform-objects.

Inputs: card #30692 (body, triage 6671686007, claims 6675467698 / 6675514573 / 6675727155, dev report 6677017944), ruling 6670372892 on #30210 (row 4 A), PR #30810 body and file list (28 files, +533/-33), the net diff against merge-base 2d04cd2b, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

- New field-group key `fieldGroups[].requiresFeature`, `z.enum(PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURE_NAMES).optional()` on `ObjectFieldGroupSchema`, the same vocabulary `ActionSchema` / `ActionParamSchema` use — RIGHT. A flag outside the registry is refused at parse with `invalid_value` at path `requiresFeature` (pinned in field-group-requires-feature.test.ts).
- Lowered output: the `.transform` on `strictObject({...})` that calls `lowerRequiresFeature(group, ctx, 'visibleWhen')` yields `visibleWhen: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'features.multiOrgEnabled != false' }` for a default-on flag and `== true` for an opt-in one (`FEATURE_GATE_OPERATORS`), and the key is stripped (`Omit` on the output type; `'requiresFeature' in out` pinned false, also inside `ObjectSchema.create`) — RIGHT. The sugar is on the input/authorable side only: `authorable-surface/data.json` gains `data/ObjectFieldGroup:requiresFeature`, the docs table and the Studio form offer it, and no parsed output, `z.infer` type or consumer ever sees it. `deriveFieldGroupLayout` / `readGroup` read `visibleWhen` only. Idempotent: the parsed group carries no key, and its `visibleWhen` envelope re-parses unchanged, so a second parse (kernel registry, stored-row replay) cannot double-lower.
- AND-combination with an authored `visibleWhen`, author first: `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` normalises a bare string to the `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` envelope BEFORE the transform runs, so the string and the envelope arms reach the same `existing.source` and both produce `(AUTHORED) && GATE` — RIGHT (both pinned equal). The `false` literal arm of the helper cannot be reached on this slot (the field-group `visibleWhen` has no boolean arm), the non-CEL and blank-source arms are reachable through an envelope and now name `visibleWhen` in their messages — RIGHT.
- `lowerRequiresFeature` third parameter `slot: RequiresFeatureSlot = 'visible'`: both action call sites (`action.zod.ts` L617 param, L2523 action) pass no slot, so actions and params are byte-unchanged — RIGHT. `RequiresFeatureSlot` is a new exported type: `api-surface/kernel.json` and `export-origins/kernel.json` each gain the one row, naming the file — RIGHT.
- `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.multiOrgEnabled.gatedInputs` gains `sys_organization.fieldGroups.group_structure`; the registry test's grammar admits `OBJECT.fieldGroups.KEY`; the platform-objects guard resolves that path to the group's `visibleWhen` and its reverse walk now books every `features.*` read in any group predicate — RIGHT, both directions.
- Lint accept-set: a field group's root verdict is now judged on `withoutLoweredFeatureGate(raw)`, which returns `undefined` when the whole source is exactly one registry flag's canonical gate, or the authored remainder when the source is `(` + authored + `) && GATE` and that remainder parses on its own; everything else is passed through untouched — RIGHT. `features` is a `SCOPE_ROOTS` member, so the follow-up `check(where, raw, ...)` on the WHOLE predicate does not bare-reference-refuse it. The finding keeps quoting the whole predicate (`celSourceOf(raw) ?? verdict.source`) and the `features`-root prescription on this slot now names `requiresFeature: 'FLAG'` — RIGHT.
- Liveness `object/fieldGroups.requiresFeature` live with in-repo evidence, state counts 77 to 78 — RIGHT. `object.form.ts` adds one row on the `fieldGroups` repeater; the four `*.metadata-forms.generated.ts` bundles carry its label and help, and the two echo-decision population pins move 122 to 124 and 732 to 733 — RIGHT.
- `sys_organization`: four groups declared in field order (`identity`, `branding`, `configuration`, `group_structure`), field `group` values retargeted from the former undeclared labels to the declared snake_case keys, `group_structure` carries `requiresFeature: 'multiOrgEnabled'`; the `System` trio stays undeclared and lands in the trailing ungrouped bucket (`deriveFieldGroupLayout` L176-208) — RIGHT, and the four `_sections` label blocks in en / zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES match the keys.
- Nothing in the diff reads `ObjectFieldGroupSchema.shape` or unwraps it, so turning it into a pipe breaks no reader; `data/object.zod.ts` importing `kernel/public-auth-features` follows the action file's own cycle-free pattern (the module is import-free).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/30692-field-group-requires-feature.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/platform-objects` minor — MATCHES the diff. Spec publishes a new optional key, a new optional helper parameter and a new exported type (additive, no removal, no tightening of an existing accept-set). Lint widens an accept-set (behaviour change, additive). Platform-objects changes the organization form and record page layout (section headers appear, two fields hide where the flag is off), additive. The changeset's `Clause-②: yes` / `Metadata-protocol: added` lines are true of the diff: one new key on a published metadata schema. The `Skills-docs:` line is true: `skills/objectstack-data/references/examples-objects.md` has a Field Groups section that teaches `fieldGroups` and `Field.group` and names neither `visibleWhen` nor `requiresFeature`; keeping it out of this diff keeps the PR off the Tier H `skills/**` row. The PR body carries the same three lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report lists no open questions. Deviations, each judged:

- `public-auth-features.ts` + tests widened into the surface — ACCEPTED. Reusing the one helper with a slot argument is the right shape (one lowering, not a twin), and the seat's re-posted claim 6675727155 names it.
- `feature-gate-guard.test.ts` — ACCEPTED. A `gatedInputs` row that the guard cannot resolve would red the guard; the resolver and the reverse walk are the enforcement half of the new row.
- `object.form.ts` — ACCEPTED. A key authors can write must be offered on the Studio form, and the authoring-surface pins would otherwise drift (the echo-decision counts are the proof).
- Liveness ledger, generated api-surface / export-origins / references — ACCEPTED, these are the `packages/spec` regeneration AGENTS.md requires before pushing.
- Translation bundles `*.objects.generated.ts` / `*.metadata-forms.generated.ts` / source hashes (not #30760's `{locale}.ts`) — ACCEPTED; section labels are keyed on the new group keys, and the disjoint file set keeps the serial constraint with #30760.
- Two echo-decision population pins — ACCEPTED; count moves that follow one new authored row in all three locales.
- Lint accepts ONLY the trailing gate the lowering emits; any other `features` read keeps its root verdict — HOLDS, and I tried to fool the peel: the removed text is always exactly one registry flag's canonical gate (the one read of `features` the renderers bind); the remainder is parsed on its own and judged in full by the same root verdict; the whole raw predicate still goes through `check()`. `GATE && record.x` (gate first), `features.X == true` on a default-on flag (wrong operator), `(current_user.x) && GATE`, `(a) && (b) && GATE` (remainder `a) && (b` does not parse so the raw is judged), `((a) && features.sso == true) && GATE` (remainder reads `features`), `(a || features.sso == true) && GATE`, `features.notAFlag`, and `features.ssoEnforced` versus the `sso` tail (different suffixes) are all still refused. A hand-written predicate byte-identical to the lowered form is accepted, as the acceptance note says, because it IS the gate. The peel cannot be used to smuggle an unbound root past the verdict.
- No `ui/**` change, per the ruling — HOLDS. `record-details.tsx` `sectionPredicateVisible` (L252) and the form's `sectionGateVisible` (`form.tsx` L110, call sites L2075 / L2169 / L3489) both evaluate a group's `visibleWhen` through `evalFieldPredicate` with `usePredicateScope()`, and `ExpressionProvider` builds that scope from its `features` prop, which `AppContent.tsx` (L1552) and `RecordFormPage.tsx` (L370) feed from `/api/v1/auth/config`. `multiOrgEnabled` is published on every deployment from the tenancy posture (`auth-manager.ts` L4655), so a single-organization deployment sees `false` and the group hides.
- Skills follow-up "noted, not filed" — see should-fix 3.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts** — HOLDS against the ruling (row 4 A: a field-group-level `requiresFeature: 'multiOrgEnabled'` lowered to the group's `visibleWhen`), against the precedent it cites (`action.zod.ts` L2523 / `action.form.ts` L182: the same helper, the same strip), and against its first consumers. Tried to break it: (a) a feature that is on at parse but off at render — the lowering is textual, nothing is evaluated at parse, the predicate is evaluated per render with the host's live `features`; correct. (b) Re-parse of a parsed object — no key survives, the envelope is stable; idempotent. (c) The strip leaving the key in an emitted surface — only input-side artifacts (authorable surface, docs table, Studio form) carry it, which is what authorable means; the parsed output type omits it. (d) A group whose fields are also placed elsewhere — membership is declared on the field and a field has one `group`, so the two organization fields cannot be in a second group; a custom form or page section that names `parent_organization_id` by field name rather than `{ group }` is outside the group gate, as every group `visibleWhen` already is, and sys_organization declares no such layout; presentation only, both fields `required: false`, so a hidden group never blocks a save. (e) The `System` trio stays undeclared: `field-group-undeclared` is a warning and the layout buckets them last, so nothing is refused. No must-fix.

**packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts** — HOLDS. One row on the `fieldGroups` repeater, help text that says what the parse does (lowered, both-hold composition, API unaffected), mirrored into the four locale bundles with the echo pins moved. Round-trip note, consistent with the action precedent: a stored object carries only the lowered `visibleWhen`, so a Studio re-open shows the gate under Visible When and an empty Requires Feature; the action form documents the same trait at L182, and the help text here says the key is lowered. Not a finding.

**packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts** — HOLDS. The slot argument defaults to `visible`, every refusal is re-worded with the slot, the registry row and the grammar extension are enforced by the guard in both directions. Two should-fixes below, neither a contract break.

Findings:

- should-fix 1 (public-auth-features.ts): `lowerRequiresFeature`'s `slot` is not tied to `T` — `T extends WithRequiresFeature` still only knows `visible`, and the read is `(rest as WithRequiresFeature & { visibleWhen?: ... })[slot]`, so a future caller passing `'visibleWhen'` on a shape that has only `visible` compiles and writes the wrong slot silently. Make the slot part of the generic constraint (a shape keyed on the slot) so the compiler refuses the mismatch.
- should-fix 2 (object.zod.ts docblock / public-auth-features.ts semantics note): the `default-on` comment promises that a missing flag "keeps the input visible". That holds on an action's `visible` (fail-soft) and not on this slot: a group predicate is fail-closed, and the console's `features` is `{}` until `/api/v1/auth/config` resolves (`AppContent.tsx` L24-L30), so a multi-organization deployment hides Group Structure for the pre-fetch window and any host that publishes no `features` hides it for good. The PR's acceptance note names the no-features host, not the pre-fetch window. State the fault direction of this slot beside the semantics table, and pin it, so the next flag gated on a group is chosen knowing it.
- should-fix 3 (process): the `Skills-docs:` follow-up is "noted, not filed" in the dev report. Prime Directive #10 lets an acceptance note carry it, but an owed skills line with no card is the kind that evaporates; the seat files the skills card before this lands or carries it on #30692 at close.

No must-fix. The `hits` files hold against the cited code, the ruling they implement and their first consumers.

Check-runs on the head at the time of this read: no gate-carrying run red; `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (aggregate) are `success`; the Test Core shards, Test UI shards, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check (workspace / consumer gates / UI / debt ledger / source gates), and the remaining Lint jobs were still `in_progress`. This record judges the diff; the seat's ACCEPT reads the finished conclusions.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `559cf50443f54565dd625a39bc3aff0e6fb1a759`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts (both `lowerRequiresFeature` call sites and the action shape's keys), packages/spec/tsconfig.test.json and packages/spec/package.json (the program that compiles the new compile-time pins), ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx (the `features` scope's lifecycle), and the two amended pins in packages/spec and packages/platform-objects.

Delta record: one commit 559cf504 on top of 24375ec4 (6 files, +105/-23), judged against the tree. The PASS of record 6677172123 on 24375ec4 is carried forward for everything this commit did not touch: object.form.ts, validate-expressions.ts and its tests, the feature-gate guard, the generated surfaces, the translation bundles and the echo pins are byte-identical between the two heads. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

- `lowerRequiresFeature` is now generic on the slot: `T extends WithRequiresFeature(S)`, `S extends RequiresFeatureSlot = 'visible'`, where `WithRequiresFeature(S)` is `{ requiresFeature? }` intersected with `{ [K in S]?: SlotPredicate }` and `{ [K in Exclude(RequiresFeatureSlot, S)]?: never }` — RIGHT. An action or param (which carries `visible`) lowered into `'visibleWhen'`, or a field group (which carries `visibleWhen`) lowered into the default `'visible'`, no longer type-checks; the two `@ts-expect-error` pins in field-group-requires-feature.test.ts hold exactly those two cases, and they are compiled: `packages/spec` `typecheck` runs `check:test-typecheck --project tsconfig.test.json`, which reaches `src/**/*.test.ts` (the build tsconfig excludes tests; the sibling exists for this), so the pins are not phantom checks.
- The read is a widening assignment, `const slotted: { [K in S]?: SlotPredicate } = input`, then `slotted[slot]` — no cast, as claimed. The value default `slot: S = 'visible' as S` does carry an assertion; it is sound in the only shape that reaches it, because `S` is `'visible'` whenever the argument is omitted and no type argument is written. A caller spelling the type argument by hand and omitting the value would lower into `visible` — a TypeScript limitation, not reachable from either schema, noted and not a finding.
- The two action call sites (`action.zod.ts` L617 param, L2523 action) are byte-unchanged and still satisfy the `'visible'` instantiation: neither the param nor the action output carries a top-level `visibleWhen` key — `visibleWhen` appears in that file only as a per-option key inside a param's `options` (L418) and as an alias row that resolves to `visible` at parse (L1067), so the `never` half of the constraint is not met by any real key. The field-group output has `visibleWhen` and no `visible` — RIGHT on both sides.
- `RequiresFeatureSlot` keeps its name and union; its public surface rows in api-surface / export-origins are unchanged — RIGHT. `SlotPredicate` and `WithRequiresFeature(S)` stay module-private.
- Fault direction stated where it is decided: the `PublicAuthFeatureSemantics` table now says "keeps the input visible" is the slot's fault direction, not the gate's; `featureGatePredicate`'s docblock scopes "fails open" to a fail-soft slot; `RequiresFeatureSlot` names both directions; the field-group `requiresFeature` docblock, the sys_organization comment and the changeset each say the group is hidden while `features` does not carry the flag and appears once it is published — RIGHT, and consistent with the slot's standing contract (ADR-0085 §5 fail-closed; `FIELD_RULE_SLOT_CONSEQUENCE` in lint says the same).
- The platform-objects pin `features not yet published: the gate faults and the group is hidden` evaluates the canonical gate with `extra: { features: {} }`, expects `ok === false`, and expects the layout without the two fields — RIGHT; it is the empty-scope reading the console's `useState({})` produces (AppContent.tsx L24-L30), so the pin measures the real shape.
- The changeset text and the PR body's `Skills-docs:` line now read `follow-up #30812`; #30812 exists, open, titled for examples-objects.md's Field Groups section, filed by the seat with the `Skills-docs` line as its gate — RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/platform-objects` minor. The delta narrows a generic constraint on an exported helper (`lowerRequiresFeature`): a hypothetical external caller passing a shape with both slots, or the wrong slot, would now fail to compile — that is the refusal the first record asked for, on a helper whose only callers are the two spec schemas, and it stays inside minor. `Clause-②: yes` / `Metadata-protocol: added` remain true; `Skills-docs: follow-up #30812` is true of the board.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev claim (1), the slot keyed on the shape — HOLDS against the tree (see ①). The pins are real; the call sites are byte-unchanged.
- Dev claim (2), fail-closed on an empty `features` scope — HOLDS and is the question put to this record: is "hidden for the session if `/auth/config` fails" acceptable under ruling 6670372892, or a must-fix? ACCEPTABLE, not a must-fix. The ruling chose the field-group `visibleWhen` as the mechanism, and that slot's fault direction is a standing contract (ADR-0085 §5: "FALSE or a faulting predicate — fail-closed — hides the WHOLE group") that this PR did not set and may not quietly reverse; the blast radius is two presentation-only, `required: false` fields on one form and one record page, readable and writable through the API, on a session whose auth config fetch has already failed (a state in which the console's login-surface flags and `create_organization` gating are equally unknown); the window on a healthy session is the pre-fetch gap, after which the group appears; and the direction is now stated at the semantics table, the predicate, the slot type, the key, the object and the changeset, and pinned. Seeding the console's `features` with the registry's defaults so a default-on flag resolves before the fetch would close the gap for every surface at once — that is `ui/**`, which the claim fences off and the ruling says needs no change; it is a candidate card for the ui lane, not a finding on this PR.
- No new files, no governed path, no `ui/**` touched — HOLDS.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts** — HOLDS. The constraint refuses the mismatch at compile time instead of writing into a key the schema never reads; the read is cast-free; the semantics prose now tells the truth about both slots. Tried to break it: an action shape with the per-option `visibleWhen` (L418) — that key lives on an option object inside `options`, not on the param, so the `never` half is not met; the alias row (L1067) is consumed by `strictObject` before the transform, so no `visibleWhen` reaches the output. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts** — HOLDS. Docblock only; the key, the transform and the output shape are unchanged from 24375ec4. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts** — untouched by the delta; PASS carried forward.

No must-fix, no should-fix on this delta. Record 6677172123's should-fix 1 and 2 are resolved by this commit; should-fix 3 is carried by #30812.

Check-runs on head 559cf504 at the time of this read: none red; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (aggregate) are `success`; Build Core, Build UI Deps, Build Docs, Live E2E UI, Plan Test Core shards, the Type Check jobs (workspace / consumer gates / source gates / debt ledger) and the remaining Lint jobs were still `in_progress`, and the Test Core / Test UI shards had not yet been planned. This record judges the diff; the seat's ACCEPT reads the finished conclusions.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-yaj4v5`
